#9368. Not Butter, Oil, Or Lard: Chicken Skin Is 10x Crispier With This Rich Ingredient

Top-notch crispy chicken skin can steal the show. Sure, flavorful and juicy meat is tasty, but encased in a mouth-watering crispiness, the poultry experience only gets better. Achieving such a crackly bite entails light seasoning, low moisture, and – especially crucially – a good dose of rendered fat. Cooks often use butter, oil, or lard to improve crisping, but for an extra-rich rendition, reach for duck fat.

This under-utilized fat source is uber-savory, all while boasting a moderate smoke point. The ingredient comes as a firm paste at room temperature, meaning you'll need to melt the fat, then spread it onto the exterior of the chicken skin. The fat offers a two-for-one punch, adding both flavor and effectively crisping the skin as your chicken roasts.

It's a technique compatible with many poultry cuts. In addition to an entire bird, you can add a touch to skin-on thighs or breasts, enhancing the dish in more subtle ways. Or dive in all the way and even fry your chicken in duck fat. In addition to chicken, you could make duck confit, cooking the protein in its own fat. Duck fat gives skin-on poultry that extra oomph, crisping up the skin to a delicious effect.

Not sure what to pair with duck fat-covered chicken? The add-in meshes with various flavors. Season and bake a whole bird with salt and pepper alongside the fat, and you've already got a mouth-watering rendition as-is. The duck fat also pairs well with herbal seasonings like dried thyme and oregano, as well as a generous dose of garlic.

You could also consider then roasting the chicken on a bed of vegetables, letting the rich fat drip down and flavor alliums and root vegetables. Or cook the bird in the same vessel as potatoes, which can be tossed in more duck fat for good measure. Roast potatoes are 10 times richer with this magical fat; in combination with the crispy chicken skin, you'll get a truly decadent meal.

The abundant richness could use some bright elements to cut through the fat. Squeeze on some lemon — both during and after the cooking process — or finish with a drizzle of balsamic. A sprinkling of parsley goes a long way, as does a crisp glass of wine, making chicken skin a special occasion.

#9361. Bakery Tourism Is Booming—These Are The 15 Spots Everyone Wants To Visit

Your next trip might come with a side of cardamom bun.

Bakeries are no longer just a stop along the way—they’re the final destination. According to Yelp’s 2027 Food and Drink Trend report, bakeries are becoming such a hot commodity that people are planning entire trips around viral treats. Yelp searches for “bakeries near me” are up 561% from last year, while searches for a “sweet treat” are up 303%. Treat yo’ self culture is officially here.

Bakery tourism is on the rise, and honestly, I'm not surprised. I, myself, am prone to walking unfamiliar city streets just to get my hands on the town's most beloved pastry. And people are getting pretty specific about what they want. Searches for cardamom buns are up 24%, kouign-amann 67%, and salt bread a whopping 616%.

It’s not just individual pastries getting all the attention, either. Yelp found that searches for “hot and new bakeries” jumped 359%, while “best gluten-free bakery” rose 113%. Bakeries are also the most-saved type of specialty food shop on Yelp’s My Lists feature. Even New York City's Radio Bakery, which you’ll find below, saw searches increase by 176%. It seems we’re all doing some serious research before our next pastry run.

So which hot spots should you add to your must-visit list? I asked Yelp to do a deep dive into the most-saved bakeries across America to see which ones people are bookmarking. Here's what came out on top.

This famed Taiwanese bakery opened its first U.S. outpost earlier this year in Pasadena, California, and has already gone viral for its unique cream cheese-filled bagels and flaky pastries.

What started out as a pandemic-era creation has now morphed into a line-worthy brick-and-mortar. Bad Butter regularly draws block-long lines, with its breads, croissants, and pastries often selling out.

In Santa Ana, California, 61hundred Bread is known for its signature heirloom blue-corn masa sourdough bread, along with Filipino baked goods like pandesal and ube-filled cruffins.

At this New York City French bakery, the jambon-beurre sandwich is the star item. Fresh baguettes and flaky croissants are also among the other reasons locals and tourists flock to the shop.

Located at the Halepuna Waikiki hotel in Honolulu, Hawaii, Halekulani Bakery is known for its signature coconut cake and assortment of pastries.

Located in Los Angeles, California, Out Of Ordi specializes in Korean-style salt bread.

New York City’s Sunday Morning frequently sells out of its viral cinnamon rolls.

San Diego’s Relic Bakery & Kitchen offers a mix of sweet and savory baked goods, from pies and croissants to breads and danishes.

In New York City, you’ll find Justin’s Salt Bread, voted the city’s best new bakery of the year and known for—you guessed it—its salt bread.

San Francisco’s Butter & Crumble is known for its crumble cakes and laminated pastries, with offerings that rotate seasonally.

Another Honolulu bakery makes the list, although this one comes with a twist. Part bakery, part butcher shop, The Local General Store sells everything from quiche and danishes to sausage and ham.

It looks like my travel schedule just got a little busier (and tastier).

#9359. 8 of our employee-owners’ favorite family recipes for the holidays  : Celebrate the season with us.

The holidays are always a big deal here at King Arthur, and this year we’re celebrating with something extra-special: our brand-new Enjoy the Bake campaign, which is all about the joy of baking together.

Enjoy the Bake is a reminder that memories are made around a mixing bowl, and traditions are passed down in the kitchen. In honor of this precious holiday baking season, our employee-owners are sharing the family-favorite recipes that mean the most to them this time of year.

“Every year since I was in grade school, my mom and I would spend the night before Thanksgiving making every type of pie that the family wants. We were a family of six, and everyone's taste was different. What makes it such a lasting memory is how much of a well-oiled machine my mom and I were when working together in the kitchen. She would make pie crust, and I would make all the fillings! Years later, we still make pies for the holidays — but in our own homes — and then come together for the holiday.”

Martina Fleurrey, Customer Experience Supervisor

Get the recipes: Apple Pie, Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, and Pumpkin Pie

“I grew up with my grandparents making giant batches of pizzelle for the holidays. Their delicate crunch and subtle hint of vanilla are things I'll always associate with the season. My dad now has the pizzelle press, and every holiday, we carry on the tradition, taking turns pouring the batter, pressing, and carefully removing each one.”

“My mom and I entered a gingerbread house contest every year, and making that together was so fun, as was shopping for the candy. More than once, our design was completely themed around a weird gummy shape we couldn't say no to. It was an opportunity to bake gingerbread in increasingly odd shapes, get creative with themes and ingredients, and channel our cheeky humor.” (Learn how to make your own gingerbread house in our new On-Demand Class: Gingerbread House Baking, Building & Decorating.)

Annabelle Shippee, Social Media Strategist

Get the recipe: Construction Gingerbread for Gingerbread Houses

“Each year on Thanksgiving my paternal grandmother, who had 10 kids, would make pies and bring them to each of her local kids. One year, she made two for us, as we were having a big gathering and pumpkin is my dad's favorite pie — one pie was for the gathering and one for just our family. My dad put his personal pumpkin pie upstairs in the closet. About a month later, I hear a screech and come running: My mom found the pie … which was now all moldy. We still laugh about that to this day. The last couple of years, I've been making our Pumpkin Cheesecake Pie as a new elevated version of my grandmother's classic pumpkin pie. It's been a fan favorite, and it's so beautiful to slice.”

Jordan Kilby, Director, Digital Marketing and Customer Data

“One of our family traditions is sausage bread on Christmas Eve. It's served as an appetizer (but to be honest, we all eat enough of it to be a full meal). This is one of my favorite family recipes, not only because it's delicious, but it's also nostalgic. My grandmother made it every year, and my Aunt Millie included it as one of the recipes to pass down in a family cookbook she created. My brother and I have baked it for many years, and now my kids are starting to take over the baking. (We are all still doing the eating.) It's so good that everyone looks forward to it — probably the reason it's lasted four generations.”

Get the recipe: The dough is similar to this Braided Stromboli recipe, using Italian sausage, parsley, and Romano cheese as the filling

“We started having Cranberry Orange Scones on Christmas morning back when I was a little kid. We'd use the King Arthur scone mix and the special scone pan; I loved pressing the dough into the wedge-shaped wells. At one point, we decided that we'd use orange juice as the liquid in the dough instead of milk for extra orange flavor, and that became our ‘secret trick’ that made the scones so delicious. Nowadays, we make the recipe from scratch (even though I still love the box mix) and have scones and coffee while we open stockings on Christmas morning. They're the perfect treat for our family — they feel special without being fussy, so we're able to mix them up and bake them fresh without taking away from our family time.”

“My mom has a late fall birthday, and since childhood she has insisted that instead of a cake she get a pumpkin pie to celebrate. So over the years, in the weeks between her birthday and Thanksgiving, my family ate a lot of pumpkin pie in all varieties: store-bought, homemade, topped with pecans and whipped cream, graham cracker crust and flaky pastry. When my sister's child was born, I went and stayed with her to hang out, clean laundry, and bake comfort food. When my mom showed up to visit, I had a batch of our Test Kitchen's pumpkin pie bars handy. Upon trying them she declared they were ‘the best pumpkin pie she had ever eaten.’ Since then, they have reigned pumpkin pie supreme and been the most requested dessert on the Dyer family holiday table.”

Cecile Dyer, Senior Video Producer, Baking Education

For the smoothest — and tastiest — holiday baking, check out our Thanksgiving Survival Guide.

#9357. Costco's Thanksgiving Dinner Kit Is Officially Back—Here's What It Comes With

The turkey, the sides, and a whole lot less holiday stress.

Depending on who you are, cooking a full Thanksgiving dinner can bring either excitement or complete dread. If you fall into the latter camp, Costco is here to help with its newest offering in the deli department.

Laura Lamb of @costcohotfinds shared on social media that the warehouse’s Thanksgiving dinner kit has officially returned for 2026. The prepared meal includes all the holiday essentials, with much of the prep work already taken care of.

Each kit comes with a seasoned half turkey breast over a bed of herbed stuffing, along with Yukon Gold mashed potatoes, green beans, cranberry sauce, and gravy. Costco is pricing the meal at just $3.99 per pound, which works out to around $40 to feed seven to eight people.

The label includes simple instructions for preparing all the components. The uncooked turkey, naturally, takes the most time. Since it’s placed over the stuffing, the turkey drippings add even more flavor and moisture as it roasts in the oven.

The warehouse keeps this dinner kit pretty consistent from year to year, although one Costco shopper wasn’t as impressed with a particular component this time around. Costco fan and content creator @photogami reports that the gravy is a bit underseasoned and not as good as it was last year. (Thankfully, this issue has a pretty easy solution.)

Lamb also noted that you’ll still need to buy a few extras to round out the meal, like dinner rolls and pumpkin pie. And if you’re a stuffing lover, the amount that comes in Costco’s kit might not be enough for you.

Still, it’s hard to argue with the price and convenience—and members are already eager to pick up a kit for their own holiday celebrations. “Got this last year and it was all absolutely delicious,” one user on Instagram wrote. “Highly recommend.” Another commented, “This is such a great idea for a smaller Thanksgiving!”

If you want to grab a kit for yourself, plan accordingly. All Costco locations are closed on Thanksgiving Day, so you only have a few days to snag one.

In my opinion, the best stuffing is made with cornbread. You bring the best of both worlds together, and it’s the perfect Thanksgiving side. We double down on the corn flavor by cutting most of the dairy and swapping in canned creamed corn for the liquid. The resulting cornbread is delicious enough to eat straight out of the pan.
